preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 500
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 500) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all('Dee' == s or 'Dum' == s for s in [stdin.split()[1] for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second value on its first line is either 'Dee' or 'Dum', indicating the starting player.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 50 for N in [int(stdin.split()[0]) for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first value on its first line is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 50) representing the number of stacks.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(B) <= 50 and all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in B) for B in [stdin.split()[0] for _ in range(T) if stdin.split()[0] != 'Dee' and stdin.split()[0] != 'Dum'])
preconditions.description: For each test case, each of the N following lines is a binary string B (1 ≤ |B| ≤ 50) representing a stack, where each character is '0' or '1'.

postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'Dee' or 'Dum', indicating the winner of the game.

postconditions.expression: all((starting_player == 'Dee' and (any(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks) and not all(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks))) or (starting_player == 'Dum' and (any(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks) and not all(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks))) or (starting_player == 'Dee' and all(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks)) or (starting_player == 'Dum' and all(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks)) or (starting_player == 'Dee' and not any(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks) and not all(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks)) or (starting_player == 'Dum' and not any(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks) and not all(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks))) == (winner == starting_player)
postconditions.description: The winner is determined by optimal play: if the starting player can force a win, they win; otherwise, the other player wins. The game is a variant of Nim where players can only remove from stacks with their respective top element ('0' for Dee, '1' for Dum). The winner is the starting player if they can make a move and the opponent cannot force a win, or if the opponent has no valid moves initially.

postconditions.expression: all((winner == 'Dee') == (not (all(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks) and starting_player == 'Dee') and not (all(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks) and starting_player == 'Dum')))
postconditions.description: If the starting player cannot make any move (all stacks have top '1' for Dee or all have top '0' for Dum), the other player wins immediately.

postconditions.expression: all((winner == 'Dee') == (starting_player == 'Dee' and any(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks) and not all(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks)) or (starting_player == 'Dum' and any(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks) and not all(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks)) or (starting_player == 'Dee' and all(B[0] == '1' for B in stacks)) or (starting_player == 'Dum' and all(B[0] == '0' for B in stacks)))
postconditions.description: The winner is determined by the initial state: if the starting player can make a move and the opponent cannot force a win, the starting player wins. If the starting player cannot make a move, the other player wins.
